_comment: NVIDIA driver -> max supported CUDA runtime, GA rows from NVIDIA's official CUDA Toolkit release notes (docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-toolkit-release-notes). Linux and Windows minimum driver versions differ for the same CUDA release, so both are recorded. Rule: wheels bundle their own CUDA runtime, so only the DRIVER floor matters (drivers are backwards compatible) -- system CUDA toolkit version is irrelevant to pip-installed frameworks.
_architectures_comment: GPU architecture -> CUDA runtime range a torch build must target to carry kernels for it. A driver new enough for a CUDA release is not sufficient: wheels only contain SASS/PTX for the architectures they were compiled for, so e.g. an RTX 50-series (sm_120) on a cu121 build fails with 'no kernel image is available for execution on the device'. Lookup uses NVIDIA's binary-compatibility rule (a cubin runs on the same major and any higher minor compute capability, docs.nvidia.com/cuda/blackwell-compatibility-guide), so 12.1 (GB10) resolves to the 12.0 row and 10.3 (B300) to the 10.0 row. Sources: CUDA 12.8 release notes (first toolkit with sm_100/sm_120); PyTorch 2.7 release blog (pytorch.org/blog/pytorch-2-7: Blackwell support, first cu128 wheels); CUDA 11.8 release notes (first with sm_89/sm_90); PyTorch 2.8 release notes and dev-discuss.pytorch.org/t/3128 + /t/3290 (sm_50-sm_60 dropped from cu128/cu129 builds, Volta dropped from cu128 in 2.11, none of them in CUDA 13 builds) -- max_cuda 12.6 is therefore the newest build that reliably still carries those kernels.
